narrative:
Your loan application was reviewed carefully, and unfortunately, we were unable to approve it at this time. The decision was based on several key factors in your financial profile that, when considered together, suggest a higher risk of difficulty repaying the loan. Here’s why this decision was made and what stood out most in your application.

First, your current financial situation played a significant role. The model noted that your checking account balance is negative, which is uncommon among approved applicants—nearly none of those who received loans had a negative balance, and most had at least some savings in their account. This raised concerns about your immediate ability to manage additional debt. While your credit history shows no prior issues—you’ve either paid off all past loans or never taken any—this positive factor wasn’t enough to offset the other risks in your profile.

Another important consideration was the purpose of your loan. You indicated that the funds would be used to purchase a new car. While this is a common reason for borrowing, the model tends to view it as a slightly riskier purpose compared to loans for essentials like home repairs or education. This doesn’t mean car loans are never approved, but in your case, it contributed to the overall assessment of risk.

The model also took into account how your application compared to others who were approved. For example, your requested loan amount of 1,082 DM is much lower than the average approved loan of nearly 2,900 DM, which might seem like a positive. However, your installment rate—the percentage of your disposable income that would go toward repayments—is higher than average at 4%, meaning a larger portion of your income would be committed to this loan. Additionally, you’ve taken out two loans with this bank already, which is more than the typical approved applicant, who usually has just one.

While some aspects of your profile were reassuring—such as your stable employment as a skilled worker for 1-4 years, owning your home, and having no other debtors—these strengths weren’t enough to balance the concerns raised by your checking account status and the purpose of the loan. The model predicted an 81% probability that this loan could present repayment challenges, which is why we had to deny the application.

To improve your chances in the future, focus on building a positive balance in your checking account, even if it’s small. Reducing your existing loan commitments or waiting until you’ve paid down some of your current debt could also help. If possible, consider whether the purchase can be delayed until your financial situation is more stable. We understand this isn’t the news you hoped for, but we encourage you to review these areas and reapply when your circumstances have improved.
